name: Singapore
summary: An island city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula. After separating from Malaysia in 1965 it became one of the world’s richest countries and busiest ports.

location.value: An island city-state off the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, about one degree north of the equator.

terrain.value: A main island and over 60 small islands; land reclamation.
terrain.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

climate.value: Equatorial: hot and humid all year, with heavy rain.
climate.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

resources.value: Almost none; its position is its resource.
resources.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

disasters.value: Haze from forest fires in Indonesia; flash floods.
disasters.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

population.value: About 6 million people, of whom about 4 million are citizens or permanent residents.
population.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

urbanisation.value: Fully urban: about 80% of residents live in public housing (HDB flats).
urbanisation.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

disease.value: SARS (2003) and COVID-19; strict public health measures.
disease.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

migration.value: A large foreign workforce, from domestic helpers to professionals.
migration.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

economicBase.value: Trade, finance, oil refining, electronics and one of the world’s busiest ports.
economicBase.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

tradeRoutes.value: On the Strait of Malacca; one of the busiest ports.

wealth.value: One of the richest countries in the world per person.
wealth.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

moneyAndTax.value: The Singapore dollar; low income taxes and a goods and services tax.
moneyAndTax.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

inequality.value: Moderate; high incomes but large gaps between top earners and low-wage workers.
inequality.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

governmentType.value: A parliamentary republic, dominated by one party since independence.
governmentType.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

keyRulers.value: Lee Kuan Yew (prime minister 1959–1990). Goh Chok Tong. Lee Hsien Loong. Lawrence Wong (since 2024).
keyRulers.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

succession.value: Regular elections, always won so far by the People’s Action Party (PAP).
succession.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

institutions.value: A strong, well-paid civil service, strict anti-corruption laws and the Housing Development Board.
institutions.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

stability.value: Very stable since the race riots of 1964 and 1969.
stability.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

eliteConflict.value: Low; leadership changes have been planned within the ruling party.
eliteConflict.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

armyAndTech.value: Compulsory national service for men; a well-equipped modern military.
armyAndTech.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

majorWars.value: None since independence; Indonesia’s “Konfrontasi” (1963–66) affected it before.
majorWars.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

territoryChange.value: Separated from Malaysia in 1965; has added about 25% to its land area by reclamation.
territoryChange.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

alliancesRivals.value: Founding member of ASEAN (1967); close ties with the US and China.
alliancesRivals.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

inventions.value: NEWater (recycled drinking water) and large-scale land reclamation.
inventions.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

scienceEducation.value: Pupils score at the top of international tests; strong universities (NUS, NTU).
scienceEducation.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

openness.value: A very open trade and investment economy.
openness.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

communicationTransport.value: The MRT train system (1987), a world-leading port and Changi Airport.

religion.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

languageWriting.value: Four official languages: English, Malay (national language), Mandarin and Tamil.
languageWriting.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

artsArchitecture.value: Marina Bay Sands, Gardens by the Bay, and shophouses of the old town.
artsArchitecture.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

socialStructure.value: Multiracial: Chinese, Malay, Indian and other communities.
socialStructure.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

sharedIdentity.value: Multiracial harmony and meritocracy are promoted as national values.
sharedIdentity.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

dailyLife.value: About 80% live in public housing flats (HDB); hawker centres for cheap meals.

neighbours.value: Malaysia (across the Johor Strait) and Indonesia.
neighbours.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

ideasReligions.value: Multiculturalism and religious harmony; Buddhism, Christianity, Islam, Taoism and Hinduism.
ideasReligions.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

colonisation.value: Raffles set up a British post in 1819.

riseSignals.value: Independence in 1965 after separating from Malaysia; export-led industrialisation.
riseSignals.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

peakPeriod.value: Still exists; among the world’s richest countries since the 1990s.
peakPeriod.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

declineSignals.value: Not applicable: still exists. Challenges include an ageing population and high costs of living.
declineSignals.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)

outcome.value: Continues today as the Republic of Singapore.
outcome.source: Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore (2009)
